findings.where: Article specimen: the list bullets, and the PDF link 'Streamlining the PPP Process…' with its underline (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: An orange-red that appears nowhere else on the page and has no job. The palette tile lists four colours and says 'no accent', and says links are house blue, but this link is orange while 'Play again' is blue. The article page therefore has two link colours, and a third hue that does not belong to the house.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for every tile to be built in the house blue and grey, with those two as the only ink. Angélique, who would have no single link colour to copy when she adds articles. A bank officer reading the article, to whom an orange link next to blue ones looks like a different kind of link or a warning.

findings.where: First screen: the blue field's diagonal stripe pattern behind everything (desktop and phone); and the same field in the texture tile and the motion sketch
findings.fault: The hero field is covered in close diagonal hatching. The ground reads busy and looks like a technical-drawing or hazard pattern, not one calm colour field. The tile's own texture swatch says 'No texture: one flat field, no grain and no gradient', and the motion sketch's field is flat. The same surface is treated three different ways, and the hero does not match what the tile says it is.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges the first screen first and named how busy or quiet the ground is as a thing to get exactly right. Mark, who finds busy sites off-putting and is not an engineer, so a hatched ground pulls him toward 'techy'.

findings.where: First screen: the ghosted 'PPP' letters in pale blue behind the heading (desktop; partly visible behind the heading on phone)
findings.fault: A second decorative layer of large translucent letters sits under the white heading, on top of the stripes. It muddies the ground behind Mark's line and adds a tone that is in no palette role.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for one soft ground, at most one borrowed detail, and no novelty. A visitor reading the heading, who sees a faint jumble of shapes behind the first words rather than a clean field.

findings.where: Nav lockup on the first screen, and the texture tile's mark: the logo reversed to white
findings.fault: The logo is shown recoloured to white. The client holds only the full-colour JPEG, and the tile presents the white version as settled ('the mark reverses to white'). It never shows that this version still needs Mark's agreement. On this blue field the full-colour logo cannot be used at all, so the whole direction depends on a version that does not exist yet.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who owns the logo and has not approved a white version. The founder, who would be choosing a direction without knowing it depends on that approval.
